steps.what: Locate the current yardmaster-issued written instruction and its car and track references in the {OPS_SYSTEM} yard work list
Receive oral or written instructions from yardmasters or yard conductors indicating track assignments and cars to be switched, read them fully and clarify or read back as required

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} yard work list to open the current issued instruction for the operator's duty and show its exact car and track references. The operator reads and clarifies the instruction; the view neither assigns tracks nor operates switches.
tasks.previous_blocker: An operator may need to navigate repeatedly to the correct issued instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native duty filters and version indicators can reduce this navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous instructions, changed conditions and read-back discipline remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: The operator challenges an instruction that does not match the yard situation.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-6 for yard access, operational review and national consultation if worker monitoring changes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a versioned yard work-list view can reduce instruction retrieval while leaving instruction interpretation and read-back manual.

assumptions: Representative episode is receipt of an existing digital written instruction. The yardmaster produces its duty, car, track, sequence and version fields during existing instruction preparation; no new structured capture is shifted to that role. If those fields do not exist, manual receipt remains and no new free feed is assumed.

S1 verifies the selected duty and current instruction; s2 retains all reading, clarification and read-back. Missing or conflicting instructions stop progression and go to the yardmaster. Receiving instructions is not executing them.

No separate acknowledgement record is established here. If actually required, split its writing and any send before estimating that episode. Purely oral receipt cannot receive this retrieval saving. Test native configuration first; existing filters earn no new gain.
Shares are provisional active effort for written receipt, not measured timings. No new staff scoring, tracking or allocation is proposed.
research_questions: Is finding the current issued instruction still a manual navigation problem?

already_counted.description: Current-instruction checking, full reading and read-back remain.

incremental.description: Check duty-filter and version display after yard configuration changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5, gross=7.5; upkeep 1 gives net 6.5. Low zero for already filtered written instructions or wholly oral instructions; do not add duplicate setup or extrapolate the written-receipt gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect rolling stock and route repairs

steps.what: Inspect tracks, cars, and engines for defects and determine observed condition at the actual equipment
Assess service needs and immediate restrictions, resolving uncertain defects and the proposed repair destination under current yard procedures
Write the actual defect and repair-routing request in the {OPS_SYSTEM} yard record and check the full description, identifiers and restrictions
Save the request in the same {OPS_SYSTEM} yard record
Check the final request against current yard routing constraints and authorize or refuse its repair dispatch
Send the authorized engines and cars for repairs by communicating the exact repair-routing request and restrictions to responsible yard staff

tasks.design: Configure exact equipment references in the {OPS_SYSTEM} defect request to avoid retyping identifiers. The operator still inspects, assesses and writes the defect and routing restriction; the yardmaster authorizes the final dispatch and the operator communicates it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defect requests may repeat equipment references already selected for inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment-linked forms can carry those exact references.
tasks.still_hard: Whether damaged rolling stock can safely move depends on real condition and current yard constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The operator identifies defects and stops unsafe work rather than trusting a completed form.

ambition.what: No automated rolling-stock movement or repair decision.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-6 for equipment data access and operational review; national consultation if applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: equipment-linked defect forms can reuse identifiers without replacing physical inspection or dispatch authority.

assumptions: Representative episode has an actual defect request and existing yardmaster dispatch authority; no new approval role is introduced to gate an author's own note. S5 is another person's real routing authorization after the final request exists. If authority differs, model the actual actor and retained effort before use.

S1 captures actual equipment identity and defects; s2 captures service needs and restrictions; s3 writes and checks all meaning. Only exact existing equipment references default. Missing or mismatched identifiers require manual reconciliation. No image classifier or structured defect feed is assumed.

S6 is the real repair dispatch communication, separate from writing and saving. Any request or restriction change voids a1 and returns to s5. Yard staff's physical movement and repair remain unchanged existing work, not software actions or transferred labour; any movement performed by this operator must be modelled as a separate retained action in that episode.

Test native forms first. Same-system save takes negligible effort, shown at minimum share 1 fully retained and ungated. Existing identifier defaults earn no new gain. Shares are hypothetical, not measured rail baselines.
unknowns: Operator versus yard staff movement duties
research_questions: Which identifiers are still manually repeated on actual defect requests?

already_counted.description: Operator inspection, assessment and full defect-request writing/check remain; yardmaster labour is excluded from this focal denominator.

incremental.description: Check equipment identifier mappings after yard system changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact saved request snapshot, identified equipment, destination and restrictions authorized in s5; any edit voids authority

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B=95 excludes yardmaster share 5; R=93.2, gross=1.8947; focal upkeep 1 gives net 0.8947. High rounds down. Low zero when equipment references already default, so no duplicate tool is introduced. No saving is assigned to the save or dispatch.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe tracks from left sides of locomotives to detect obstructions on tracks, maintaining attention to the actual route and visibility

tasks.design: Keep actual track observation with the operator. No {OPS_SYSTEM} view or document template changes the visual detection work in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on real-time visibility and attention.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced software change removes this observation work.
tasks.still_hard: Occlusion, movement and changing conditions make remote records insufficient.
tasks.human_edge: The operator sees the actual hazard in its immediate context.

ambition.what: No replacement of the lookout function.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a record view does not replace actual visual observation for track obstructions.

assumptions: Boundary is actual visual lookout. No record write, report or signal is specified as part of this observation statement. Actual hazard communication or intervention, when required, must be split into its own retained action rather than hidden here; signalling is separately covered by 23786.

A native record or template cannot reduce the visual scan. No camera feed, detector or reliable obstruction labels are assumed. If the actual duty includes a log, split and evaluate that writing before retaining a zero for the expanded episode.
The single share denotes the defined task, not an invented timing baseline. No transferred work or new system is proposed; incremental upkeep is zero for that reason.
unknowns: Whether a concrete duty includes a separate observation log
research_questions: Are any real recording duties attached to this observation episode?

incremental.description: No system or workflow change is proposed, so no incremental upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and upkeep=0. Templates and native views do not alter the physical observation; a separate actual log would require a different decomposition.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify current car movement, worker positions, agreed instruction and readiness before signalling a brake or switch action
Signal other workers to set brakes and to throw track switches when switching cars from trains to way stations, using the agreed real-time signals and confirming understanding

tasks.design: Retain live readiness checking and brake or switch signalling with the rail switch operator. A {OPS_SYSTEM} record cannot replace the current physical conditions on which the signal depends.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signals must match the actual movement and current worker positions.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced change removes this live communication effort.
tasks.still_hard: Conditions can change between readiness and the signal.
tasks.human_edge: The operator withholds or changes the signal when the actual movement is unsafe.

ambition.what: No autonomous brake or switch instruction.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live yard signals depend on current physical readiness, not merely an earlier stored switching instruction.

assumptions: The gate is the operator's actual immediate movement-readiness decision, not self-approval of an authored document or an ordinary save. It authorizes only the exact next signal under the conditions checked in s1; changed conditions require another check.

Signal communication is separate from the readiness judgement. It is active coordination, not a negligible filing tail. Other workers' physical braking and switch operation are unchanged existing duties, excluded from focal labour; no work is transferred to them by this design.

No separate record write is established by this statement. If the actual operator must enter a signal log, split its actual writing and evaluate native fields before estimating that expanded workflow. A template does not reduce either live step here.
Shares are provisional decomposition, not measured signal timings. No new system is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual signal protocol and any separate logging duty
research_questions: Does the concrete signalling episode include any independent record entry?

already_counted.description: Immediate physical readiness checks are already retained before the signal.

incremental.description: No new system or process, so no incremental upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Exact next brake or switch signal under physical conditions checked in s1; changed conditions void readiness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and upkeep=0. Both the live readiness decision and the actual signal remain; no record operation or equipment automation has been shown to change them.

role.altitude: Written instruction retrieval and equipment-reference repetition may shrink; observation, defect judgement and live signalling remain.
reach: Yardmaster: learn instruction version control and dispatch authority boundaries.
skills_to_grow: Separate record completion from operational authority
role.ambitious_version: An operator with clear current instructions and equipment-linked defect records who retains live observation and movement communication.
